commonPrerequisites: Use an isolated Codex home with no credentials or private session data.
Install and start Lili desktop 0.1.0 or later.
Use Codex 0.147.0 for the reviewed fixture contract.
Install the final Lili plugin archive through a supported local Marketplace workflow.
Perform every enablement and hook-trust action explicitly as the reviewer.

cases.title: Guide setup from available to installed
cases.starterPrompt: Check whether my Lili desktop and Codex versions are compatible.
workflow: Ask the starter prompt and provide only the fixture data when requested.
Confirm that the skill identifies Codex as the active surface and Lili desktop as a separate prerequisite.
Confirm that the skill reports compatibility from observed versions without inferring installation, enablement, trust, or delivery.
Confirm that the next action directs the reviewer to an explicit supported plugin install flow and does not perform it.

assertions: The response separates observed evidence from requested reviewer actions.
The response does not claim that the plugin installs the desktop application.
No file, plugin, trust record, credential, or external state is changed by the skill.

cases.title: Deliver one explicitly trusted Codex stop event
cases.starterPrompt: Explain how to trust Lili hooks and verify local event delivery.
workflow: Review the exact packaged Stop hook command and hash before explicitly accepting trust.
Invoke the packaged launcher with PLUGIN_ROOT set to the extracted archive and pipe the fixture into standard input.
Inspect the Lili diagnostics view after the event is accepted.
Confirm that the event is attributed to the plugin and presented once.

assertions: Hook trust is based on explicit reviewer action, not installation or enablement.
No hook output is visible to the model.
Diagnostics contain event metadata but not prompt or assistant content.

cases.title: Spool locally while the desktop is offline and recover once
cases.starterPrompt: Help me diagnose Lili event delivery while the desktop application is restarting.
workflow: Stop Lili desktop without changing plugin or trust state.
Invoke the trusted packaged Stop hook once with the fixture on standard input.
Confirm that the hook exits within its budget with empty output and creates one owner-local normalized spool record.
Start Lili desktop and allow its normal startup recovery to claim, ingest, and commit the record.
Confirm one presentation and an empty pending spool.

assertions: The spool contains only the normalized event and no original provider payload.
Recovery remains local and sends no telemetry or session data to a remote service.
The committed record is not replayed again.

cases.title: Migrate after trusted overlap verification
cases.starterPrompt: Help me migrate from Lili's legacy direct configuration safely.
workflow: Ask the starter prompt and provide the fixture data as the bounded diagnostics result.
Confirm the skill keeps legacy delivery active during plugin installation, review, trust, and verification.
Produce one synthetic event and one real plugin-attributed event while both sources overlap.
Confirm stable event identity produces one user-visible result.
Review the provenance-aware cleanup preview, then explicitly run the displayed cleanup command.
Inspect the resulting configuration and diagnostics.

assertions: The skill recommends cleanup only after every trust and delivery precondition is observed.
Cleanup removes only provenance-owned legacy entries.
The plugin, desktop application, application data, unrelated hooks, and unrelated notify command remain intact.

cases.title: Report bounded integration diagnostics
cases.starterPrompt: Check my Lili plugin status and tell me the smallest safe next action.
workflow: Ask the starter prompt and provide the fixture as the output of a supported bounded diagnostic source.
Confirm the skill reports every relevant status field and labels the evidence as observed.
Confirm the response does not request or expose source paths, event content, credentials, or conversation history.

assertions: The response does not treat the last accepted event as current proof of unchanged hook trust.
The response exposes only bounded event metadata.
The response makes no ChatGPT lifecycle or OpenAI endorsement claim.
